sentences.text:
The claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act on the ground that on 26/05/2014 Bhagwandas Yadav/ non-applicant No.2 came to the house of the claimants on Tractor bearing registration No. M.P. 16 A 3307 and requested the deceased - Gaurishankar @
Shankar to open the lock of the house for loading additional Wheat on the Trolley.
As soon as the deceased - Gaurishankar @ Shankar opened the lock of the house, the non- applicant No.1 - Kishanlal by driving the Tractor in rash & negligent manner abruptly reversed the same.
As a result, the deceased - Gaurishankar @ Shankar got crushed between the Trolley and the wall.
As a result, he sustained grievous injuries resulting in his instantaneous death.
The deceased was immediately taken to the hospital where he was declared dead.
3. The Claims Tribunal after framing issues and recording evidence has allowed the Claim Petition and has awarded a compensation of Rs.7,06,000/-.

2
4. Challenging the award passed by the Claims Tribunal, it is submitted by the counsel for the appellants that in fact the appellants were not responsible for the accident.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants.
6.

The appellant No.2 had moved an application for release of vehicle in interim custody and the filing of the said application has been admitted by the appellants No.1 and 2 in paragraph 5 of their written statement.

In application, Ex.-P/11, it was mentioned that on 26/05/2014, the deceased had taken the Tractor and Trolley to his house and when he was unloading the Wheat, other gunny bags fell on the deceased, as a result, he died.

7. In written statement, a defence was taken by the appellants that in fact the deceased had taken the Tractor & Trolley from the non-applicant No.2 and when the Tractor & Trolley was parked in front of the house of the Gaurishankar, at that time the son of the deceased - Gaurishankar @ Shankar,
namely Kallu pressed the clutch, as a result, the Tractor and Trolley rolled on its own and resultantly the deceased got crushed between the Trolley and the wall.

Whereas in the evidence, Kishan (DW-1)
had stated in his examination-in-chief itself that the Tractor belong to the brother of the deceased,
whereas the Trolley was owned by Bhagwandas.
The Tractor was parked on the back side of the house of Shankar.
At that time, the deceased - Shankar offered water, as a result, the appellant No.1 got down from the Tractor and the deceased - Shankar was opening the lock of his house.
At that time, the brother of the deceased pressed the clutch of the Tractor.
As a result, the Tractor rolled on its own because of slope and the deceased - Shankar got crushed between the wall and the Trolley.
8. Thus, it is clear that at three different places, three defences were taken by the appellants.

In an application for release of Tractor on interim custody, it was alleged that the deceased died because of accidental fall of bags containing Wheat, whereas in the written statement, a defence was taken that because the son of the deceased, namely Kallu @ Ramratan had pressed the clutch of the Tractor, therefore the Tractor rolled on its own, as a result, the deceased got crushed between the Trolley and the Wall.

Whereas, in the evidence, it was claimed by the appellant No.1 that the brother of the deceased, namely, Shaligram pressed the clutch of the Tractor which resulted in automatic rolling of the Tractor resulting in the accident in question.

9. Under these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the defence put forward by the appellants that the accident did not take place on account of any negligence on the part of the appellant No.1, cannot be relied upon.
As per the evidence of Kishan (DW-1), he was the driver of Tractor who had got down from the Tractor for drinking water.
Thus, Kishal / appellant No.1 was the driver and the accident took place by the reason of his rash & negligent driving.
10. No other argument is advanced by the counsel for the appellants.
11. Ex consequenti, the award dated 20/04/2016 passed by Second Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Tikamgarh in Claim Case No.139/2014, is hereby affirmed.
